title: ISMS_SCOPE
universal_lens: The ISMS scope defines a bounded operator algebra over production state spaces. In-scope assets form a closed subspace under governed decision operators, while out-of-scope dependencies act as boundary conditions. Compliance is the spectral projection of system states onto an admissible control manifold.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats the draft ISMS as a conformal prediction set for security posture. The in-scope boundary establishes the calibration domain for control observables (e.g., `CTL-ACC-001`). Out-of-scope third-party risks are modeled as latent confounders requiring non-conformity score adjustments to maintain valid coverage guarantees.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the ISMS acts as a situational constraint solver. The governed-receipts subsystem dictates valid state transitions for automated agents. The compliance monitor continuously evaluates the current system configuration against the defined scope, vetoing any transition that violates the established control library boundaries.

primitives.name: ISMS Domain Boundary Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Purpose Defines the boundary of the Information Security Management System (ISMS) for Beexly/Sports (Galaxy Sports Edge): what is in scope for the controls in `packages/compliance/src/control-library.ts`, and what is explicitly out of scope pending future work.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: System state space (dimensionless), B: Characteristic function of the ISMS boundary (boolean).
primitives.assumptions: The system state space S can be cleanly partitioned into disjoint in-scope and out-of-scope subspaces without ambiguity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when organizational changes introduce hybrid assets that straddle the defined boundary, causing topological leakage.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the GSE constraint manifold defining allowable agent actions. The boundary operator B(S) = 1 iff the state is subject to the control library.
layer2.telemetry: Coverage percentage of production assets mapped to the control library.

primitives.name: Governed Receipt Decision Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Agent/automation systems that make governed decisions on behalf of the platform (the governed-receipts admit/refuse decision surface, once merged), and the CI/CD pipeline that deploys production changes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D: Decision surface (admit/refuse boolean), A: Agent action space (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: All automated platform decisions pass through a centralized, loggable decision surface D.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if shadow IT or unmerged branches execute state mutations outside the governed-receipts kernel.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSE state-transition validator. Every CI/CD deployment or agent action must yield a valid receipt to update the global compliance state.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of automated deployments producing valid governed receipts versus manual overrides.

primitives.name: External Dependency Veto Condition
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Out of scope (draft — pending future ISMS work) - Physical security of any office or data-center facility (cloud provider physical security is inherited/relied-upon, not independently assessed here).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P_cloud: Cloud provider physical security state (binary), R_inherit: Reliance coefficient (dimensionless, 0..1).
primitives.assumptions: The cloud provider's physical security posture remains above a minimum acceptable threshold, allowing safe inheritance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if the cloud provider suffers a catastrophic physical breach, invalidating the reliance assumption and collapsing the inherited security model.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI latent confounder modeling. External dependencies are treated as fixed boundary conditions until a supplier-risk input triggers a re-evaluation of the entire conformal prediction set.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of supplier risk attestation updates and manual snapshot verifications.

reasoning_traces.think:
The ISMS scope statement functions as a rigorous mathematical partition of the Galaxy Sports Edge operational manifold. We define the total system state space \mathcal{S} and introduce a characteristic boundary operator \chi_{\text{ISMS}}: \mathcal{S} \rightarrow \{0,1\}. The 'in-scope' declaration (Quote 3, 4) establishes the primary subspace \mathcal{S}_{\text{prod}} where the control library \mathcal{C} acts as a projection operator. Any state vector s \in \mathcal{S}_{\text{prod}} must satisfy \forall c \in \mathcal{C}, c(s) = \text{compliant}. The 'governed-receipts' primitive (Quote 5) introduces a dynamic kernel K acting on the agent action space. This kernel ensures that every state transition \Delta s induced by automation is accompanied by a cryptographic proof of governance. Without this receipt, the transition is rejected, preserving the integrity of \mathcal{S}_{\text{prod}}. Conversely, the 'out-of-scope' declarations (Quote 8, 9) define the orthogonal complement \mathcal{S}_{\text{ext}}. These externalities, such as cloud provider physical security, are treated as exogenous boundary conditions. The system assumes these boundaries remain stable (Quote 11). If an external dependency fails, it constitutes a boundary condition violation rather than an internal control failure. The epistemic trace reveals a dual-layer architecture: an inner layer of strict, algorithmic enforcement (CI/CD, governed receipts) and an outer layer of probabilistic reliance on third-party attestations. The draft status (Quote 1, 14) implies the boundary operator \chi_{\text{ISMS}} is currently a soft constraint, subject to refinement as the feature branches merge.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This scoping methodology descends from the formal verification traditions of operating system kernels, specifically the separation of trusted computing bases (TCB). Historically, ISO 27001 evolved from qualitative checklists into quantifiable control frameworks. The 'governed-receipts' concept mirrors the zero-knowledge proof lineage in distributed systems, ensuring accountability without exposing full state. The reliance on cloud provider attestations reflects the modern shift toward supply-chain cryptography, where trust is mathematically delegated rather than physically verified.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two opposing decision actors: the Platform Automaton and the Adversarial Subprocessor. The Platform Automaton seeks to maximize deployment velocity while strictly adhering to the governed-receipts kernel; its utility function penalizes any state transition lacking a compliance signature. The Adversarial Subprocessor (or compromised cloud node) aims to exploit the 'out-of-scope' blind spots. It attempts to inject malicious states through the inherited physical security layer, knowing the internal ISMS controls cannot retroactively audit the hardware level. The ISMS scope acts as the Nash equilibrium boundary between these actors.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring the telemetry from the Compliance Control Monitor (Quote 7) is not perfectly correlated with the CI/CD success metrics. If deployment frequency spikes without a proportional increase in governed receipts, a veto is triggered. Leakage occurs if privileged account access (Quote 6) bypasses the standard identity provider integration, relying instead on manual snapshots. The cross-layer veto condition mandates that any manual override of the MFA state must immediately freeze the governed-receipts kernel until the discrepancy is resolved, preventing silent degradation of the security boundary.
